items.title: Harrison Barnes Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: A fellow by the name of Mr. Gilbert... He had it in charge... So they asked me to play one day... So I had been playing... So when I went there, they told me that, they kept me on the trombone.

ctx.x: Who was the leader, the boss of the whole band?

A fellow by the name of Mr. Gilbert, you know. He had it in charge, so he said he's going to run a test. He run a test. He was going to run a test. And put the music up, you know. And the music wasn't all that hard. And a whole lot of fellows couldn't make, didn't know nothing at all. And a week or so they cut the band down to about 70-something. They stayed in on trombone. Frankie Duesen still there? They passed him some kind of way they liked him, you know. Then again, Frankie Bluffey, if he hear something…
And they got a, my dad didn't know what he was doing.
